title: Prime cyclic detection after forgetting geometric-point coefficients
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $K$ an algebraically closed field, $X,Y$ schemes, $e:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $h:Y\to X$ with $h$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $n\ne0$ be a natural number with $n=0$ in $\Lambda$, $q\in\mathbf Z$, and $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $(\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\mathrm{et}}$. If the degree-$q$ base-change target $H^q(Rh_*Le^*(F[0]))$ [sbc-def-base-change-map, def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is nonzero, there is a prime $r\mid n$ which is not a unit in $\Lambda$ and for which $R^qh_*(\underline{P_r/(r)})$ is nonzero, where $P_r=\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf F_r)$ and the underline denotes the constant sheaf of $P_r$-modules [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf].

source.place: Tag 0F08 (proof, cyclic-coefficient reduction); Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree); Tag 0739 (lemma-colimit), with the arbitrary-ring coefficient argument explicitly supplied here

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-algebraically-closed-etale-sheaf-constant], applied to the underlying sheaf of sets and its additive and scalar operations, $F$ is the constant sheaf of a $\Lambda$-module $M$. Exact inverse image carries $F[0]$ to the constant $M$-sheaf in degree zero. An injective module resolution is underlying-abelian acyclic by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-module-direct-image-acyclic]. Hence its pushforward computes the abelian derived direct image as well. The underlying constant abelian sheaf is identified by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-sheaf-underlying].

The equation $n=0$ in $\Lambda$ kills $M$. Its primary components are a finite internal direct sum by [lem-sc-coprime-torsion-decomposition]. Every component is a filtered union of finitely generated subgroups; these are finite because they have bounded exponent (Mathlib AddCommGroup.finite_of_fg_isAddTorsion). The finite abelian group structure theorem (AddCommGroup.equiv_directSum_zmod_of_finite) writes them as finite sums of cyclic prime-power groups. Every prime occurring divides $n$. A component at $r$ is zero if $r$ is a unit in $\Lambda$, since multiplication by a power of $r$ is both invertible and zero there.

If every nonunit prime $r\mid n$ has zero degree-$q$ higher direct image on the constant $\mathbf F_r$-sheaf, induction using the cyclic short exact sequences $0\to\mathbf Z/r^{k-1}\to\mathbf Z/r^k\to\mathbf Z/r\to0$ and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] shows the same for all prime-power cyclic sheaves. Finite additivity gives the result for each finite subgroup. Higher direct image commutes with their filtered unions by [lemma-weil-pbc-direct-image-filtered-colimit], since $h$ is qcqs. Thus the image for $M$ is zero, contrary to the assumption. Negative degrees vanish for derived direct image of a sheaf.

Choose a prime witnessing the failure of the previous universal vanishing. In $P_r=\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf F_r)$ the ideal $(r)$ is zero, so the constant sheaf with value $P_r/(r)$ has underlying abelian sheaf $\mathbf F_r$. Apply the same module/abelian comparison as in step 1 and reflection of zero by forgetting coefficients. This gives the displayed nonvanishing for $P_r$, together with primality, divisibility and noninvertibility.
